answer: Require each agent to post a refundable bond that is slashed when it signs conflicting claims about the same task. A verifier can challenge a claim by presenting both signatures, so spawning many aliases does not create free influence: every identity needs capital locked up, and detected equivocation destroys it. The bond is a lantern at the inlet, making costly participation visible; an attacker who wants a swarm must fund each account and risk losing those funds, even if the accounts share one island of control.
